requirements.quote:
For secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1, ECDH calculations (including
   parameter and key generation as well as the shared secret
   calculation) are performed according to [IEEE1363] using the
   ECKAS-DH1 scheme with the identity map as the key derivation function
   (KDF), so that the shared secret is the x-coordinate of the ECDH
   shared secret elliptic curve point represented as an octet string.
requirements.condition: when using secp256r1, secp384r1, or secp521r1
requirements.required_behavior: perform ECDH parameter generation according to IEEE 1363 using ECKAS-DH1
requirements.why_checkable: The curve-parameter generation path can be inspected for the specified IEEE 1363 ECKAS-DH1 construction.

requirements.quote:
For secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1, ECDH calculations (including
   parameter and key generation as well as the shared secret
   calculation) are performed according to [IEEE1363] using the
   ECKAS-DH1 scheme with the identity map as the key derivation function
   (KDF), so that the shared secret is the x-coordinate of the ECDH
   shared secret elliptic curve point represented as an octet string.
requirements.condition: when using secp256r1, secp384r1, or secp521r1
requirements.required_behavior: perform ECDH key generation according to IEEE 1363 using ECKAS-DH1
requirements.why_checkable: Generated key pairs can be checked against the specified IEEE 1363 ECKAS-DH1 construction.

requirements.quote:
For secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1, ECDH calculations (including
   parameter and key generation as well as the shared secret
   calculation) are performed according to [IEEE1363] using the
   ECKAS-DH1 scheme with the identity map as the key derivation function
   (KDF), so that the shared secret is the x-coordinate of the ECDH
   shared secret elliptic curve point represented as an octet string.
requirements.condition: when using secp256r1, secp384r1, or secp521r1
requirements.required_behavior: perform the ECDH shared-secret calculation according to IEEE 1363 using ECKAS-DH1
requirements.why_checkable: Known key pairs can check the shared-secret calculation against IEEE 1363 ECKAS-DH1.

requirements.quote:
For secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1, ECDH calculations (including
   parameter and key generation as well as the shared secret
   calculation) are performed according to [IEEE1363] using the
   ECKAS-DH1 scheme with the identity map as the key derivation function
   (KDF), so that the shared secret is the x-coordinate of the ECDH
   shared secret elliptic curve point represented as an octet string.
requirements.condition: when using ECKAS-DH1 with secp256r1, secp384r1, or secp521r1
requirements.required_behavior: use the identity map as the ECDH key derivation function
requirements.forbidden_behavior: apply a different KDF within the ECDH calculation
requirements.why_checkable: The bytes emitted by ECDH can be compared directly with the point coordinate before the TLS key schedule.

requirements.quote:
For secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1, ECDH calculations (including
   parameter and key generation as well as the shared secret
   calculation) are performed according to [IEEE1363] using the
   ECKAS-DH1 scheme with the identity map as the key derivation function
   (KDF), so that the shared secret is the x-coordinate of the ECDH
   shared secret elliptic curve point represented as an octet string.
requirements.condition: when calculating the ECDH shared secret for secp256r1, secp384r1, or secp521r1
requirements.required_behavior: represent the x-coordinate of the ECDH shared-secret point as the shared-secret octet string
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use another coordinate or the complete point as the shared-secret octet string
requirements.why_checkable: Known points can verify that the shared-secret bytes encode exactly the x-coordinate.

requirements.quote:
Note that this octet string ("Z" in IEEE 1363 terminology) as output
   by FE2OSP (the Field Element to Octet String Conversion Primitive)
   has constant length for any given field; leading zeros found in this
   octet string MUST NOT be truncated.
requirements.condition: when encoding ECDH shared secret Z for a given field
requirements.required_behavior: produce a constant-length octet string for that field
requirements.why_checkable: Test vectors with differently sized x-coordinate values can verify a fixed output length.

requirements.quote:
Note that this octet string ("Z" in IEEE 1363 terminology) as output
   by FE2OSP (the Field Element to Octet String Conversion Primitive)
   has constant length for any given field; leading zeros found in this
   octet string MUST NOT be truncated.
requirements.condition: when the FE2OSP output for an ECDH shared secret begins with zero octets
requirements.forbidden_behavior: truncate leading zero octets from the shared secret
requirements.why_checkable: A shared secret with a leading-zero x-coordinate directly tests preservation of those octets.

requirements.quote:
The public key to put into the KeyShareEntry.key_exchange
      structure is the result of applying the ECDH scalar multiplication
      function to the secret key of appropriate length (into scalar
      input) and the standard public basepoint (into u-coordinate point
      input).
requirements.condition: when constructing KeyShareEntry.key_exchange for X25519 or X448
requirements.required_behavior: place the ECDH scalar-multiplication result in KeyShareEntry.key_exchange
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized key-share bytes can be compared with the result returned by the scalar-multiplication operation.

requirements.quote:
The public key to put into the KeyShareEntry.key_exchange
      structure is the result of applying the ECDH scalar multiplication
      function to the secret key of appropriate length (into scalar
      input) and the standard public basepoint (into u-coordinate point
      input).
requirements.condition: when generating an X25519 or X448 public key for KeyShareEntry.key_exchange
requirements.required_behavior: use a secret key of the appropriate curve-specific length as the scalar input
requirements.why_checkable: The scalar input length can be inspected or tested at the multiplication boundary.

requirements.quote:
The public key to put into the KeyShareEntry.key_exchange
      structure is the result of applying the ECDH scalar multiplication
      function to the secret key of appropriate length (into scalar
      input) and the standard public basepoint (into u-coordinate point
      input).
requirements.condition: when generating an X25519 or X448 public key for KeyShareEntry.key_exchange
requirements.required_behavior: use the standard public basepoint as the u-coordinate input
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use a nonstandard point as the public-key-generation basepoint
requirements.why_checkable: The point input to scalar multiplication can be compared with the curve's standard basepoint.

requirements.quote:
The ECDH shared secret is the result of applying the ECDH scalar
      multiplication function to the secret key (into scalar input) and
      the peer's public key (into u-coordinate point input).
requirements.condition: when calculating an X25519 or X448 ECDH shared secret
requirements.required_behavior: use the ECDH scalar-multiplication result as the shared secret
requirements.why_checkable: Known X25519 and X448 vectors can verify that the scalar-multiplication result is selected as the shared secret.

requirements.quote:
The ECDH shared secret is the result of applying the ECDH scalar
      multiplication function to the secret key (into scalar input) and
      the peer's public key (into u-coordinate point input).
requirements.condition: when calculating an X25519 or X448 ECDH shared secret
requirements.required_behavior: use the local secret key as the scalar input
requirements.why_checkable: The scalar operand can be inspected at the ECDH multiplication boundary.

requirements.quote:
The ECDH shared secret is the result of applying the ECDH scalar
      multiplication function to the secret key (into scalar input) and
      the peer's public key (into u-coordinate point input).
requirements.condition: when calculating an X25519 or X448 ECDH shared secret
requirements.required_behavior: use the peer's public key as the u-coordinate input
requirements.why_checkable: The point operand can be inspected or varied to verify that it comes from the peer key share.

requirements.quote:
The output
      is used raw, with no processing.
requirements.condition: after X25519 or X448 scalar multiplication produces the ECDH shared secret
requirements.forbidden_behavior: apply additional processing to the shared-secret output before using it
requirements.why_checkable: The value passed to the TLS key schedule can be compared byte-for-byte with the scalar-multiplication output.

requirements.quote:
For these curves, implementations SHOULD use the approach specified
   in [RFC7748] to calculate the Diffie-Hellman shared secret.
requirements.condition: when calculating a Diffie-Hellman shared secret for X25519 or X448
requirements.why_checkable: The curve implementation can be identified and validated against RFC 7748 test vectors.

requirements.quote:
Implementations MUST check whether the computed Diffie-Hellman shared
   secret is the all-zero value and abort if so, as described in
   Section 6 of [RFC7748].
requirements.condition: after computing an X25519 or X448 Diffie-Hellman shared secret
requirements.required_behavior: check whether the complete shared secret is the all-zero value
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use the shared secret without performing the all-zero check
requirements.why_checkable: An all-zero test vector can verify that the check is executed before key-schedule use.

requirements.quote:
Implementations MUST check whether the computed Diffie-Hellman shared
   secret is the all-zero value and abort if so, as described in
   Section 6 of [RFC7748].
requirements.condition: when the computed X25519 or X448 Diffie-Hellman shared secret is all zero
requirements.forbidden_behavior: continue the handshake using the all-zero shared secret
requirements.error_behavior: abort when the all-zero shared secret is detected
requirements.why_checkable: A peer public key producing an all-zero result can verify that the handshake does not continue.

requirements.quote:
If implementors use an alternative
   implementation of these elliptic curves, they SHOULD perform the
   additional checks specified in Section 7 of [RFC7748].
requirements.condition: when using an alternative implementation of X25519 or X448
requirements.required_behavior: perform the additional checks specified in Section 7 of RFC 7748
requirements.why_checkable: The alternative curve path can be inspected for the referenced input-validation checks and exercised with invalid inputs.
